call_points.text: Management expects a normal monsoon next year to drive a significant recovery in the sector.
New products launched in FY27 contributed approximately ₹100 Cr to revenue during the kharif season.
Herbicide prices in North India are already under significant pressure before the start of the rabi season.
Company expects to generate free cash flow by year-end as it moderates purchases and normalizes inventory.
Other expenses include fees related to the ongoing search for right M&A opportunities.
Sector margins expected stable to soft; volumes may shrink on lower acreage.
Summer sowing as of end-March 2026 is down 4.7% YoY, with rice down 7.1% and oilseeds down 6.1%.
Healthy cash and liquid balance of ₹541 Cr as of 31 March 2026; inventory slightly elevated YoY.
Annual capacity utilisation improved in FY26 versus FY25, with record production levels achieved.
Three new molecules identified for B2B, to be introduced over the next 2-3 years, with registration running in parallel.
Aquafeed venture remains at an experimental stage; products are outsourced and no investment figure has been decided.
Acephate faces a structural challenge as raw material suppliers compete with Rallis in American markets.
Even if the war ends, management says unwinding the supply chain will take 3-4 months, so Kharif costs are locked in.
Q4 gross margin was helped by a CSM contract clause paying benefit when volumes fall below thresholds.

operating_notes.text: FY26 exceptional items of -₹26 Cr include a ₹40 Cr incremental gratuity charge from the four Labour Codes notified on 21 November 2025, partly offset by ₹14 Cr profit on sale of flats and freehold land.
Agri inputs segment FY26 result was ₹217 Cr on ₹2,876 Cr revenue; Q4 segment result was -₹33 Cr.
The company has no subsidiary, associate or joint venture as on 31 March 2026.
Q4 volume growth in Crop Care was at 5%, and in Seeds was at 8% with price growth of 0% and 15%, respectively.
FY26 B2C herbicide business up 15%, fungicide up 5% and insecticide down 3%, giving 5% overall B2C growth.
Q4FY26 exports fell 33% to ₹77 Cr on Metribuzin and Pendimethalin volume and revenue decline, while CSM grew 59% to ₹66 Cr.
Soil and plant health business has reached a scale of ₹50 Cr plus and is being considered for further investment.
New products launched in FY27 contributed ₹100 Cr to revenue during the kharif season.
CSM revenue grew 12x to ₹27 Cr in Q2FY27, driven by PEKK sales volumes.
Cotton market has shrunk to 10-10.5 million hectares from a peak of 13 million, with illegal seeds capturing ~30% of the market.

timeline.summary: Q4FY26 results (standalone): revenue ₹456 Cr (+6.0% YoY), net loss ₹15 Cr (against a loss of ₹32 Cr a year earlier).
Rallis India reported FY26 revenue of ₹2,897 crore and a record EBITDA of ₹362 crore on 27 April 2026.
Sariga P Gokul, CFO, shared the audio recording of the Analysts/Investors Call on Q4FY26 results, approved by the Board on April 27, 2026, via link.
Rallis India's 28 April 2026 Q4/FY26 call transcript: FY26 revenue ₹2,897 Cr (+9%), Q4 EBITDA ₹-1 Cr; management guided seeds to mid-teen FY27 growth and flagged 15-25% input cost inflation.
Rallis India Limited’s Board recommended ₹3 dividend per share (300%) on April 27, 2026; Record Date set for June 4, 2026, with payment by June 25, 2026.
Q2FY27 results (standalone): revenue ₹858 Cr (-0.3% YoY), net profit ₹85 Cr (-16.7% YoY).
Rallis India reported Q2FY27 standalone revenue of ₹858 Cr and net profit of ₹85 Cr, impacted by weak monsoon conditions and seed returns.
Link to audio recording of Analysts/Investors Call on Unaudited Financial Results for Q2 and H1 ended September 30, 2026 held on Friday, October 23, 2026.
Rallis India reported flat Q2FY27 revenue of ₹858 Cr and a 17% drop in PAT to ₹85 Cr, citing weak monsoon impact on seeds and domestic crop protection.
Rallis India received a give effect order dropping an income tax demand of ₹408 Cr for AY 2022-23 and granting a refund of ₹8.31 Cr.

watchlist.response: CFO gave only a rough 20% SPH / 80% crop protection split and said details would be shared separately.
watchlist.text: Analyst asked for the crop protection component within the ₹255 Cr B2C sales for Q4

watchlist.response: Management said all new supplies are at higher prices but carryover inventory bought at lower prices will take time to exhaust; no quantified split given.
watchlist.text: Analyst pressed on how much of the 15-25% cost increase is being passed through versus absorbed

watchlist.response: Management said it is not building inventory beyond Kharif and will only buy what it can sell.
watchlist.text: Analyst asked whether high-cost inventory could be stranded if crude falls within 3-6 months

watchlist.response: Attributed to higher procurement prices, deliberate surplus seed production to avoid past shortages, and slower liquidation due to erratic rains.
